title: Hour-capped pod staffing with course recency
scenario: Staff ten projects by descending priority number. Contributors can take several projects while weekly hours last; eligibility needs locale, hours, and every listed course passed on the most recent attempt. The report lists multi-project contributors and course demand.

verified.why_correct: The `>=` looks like it should be `>`, but rule 1 says that on equal dates the attempt further down the file counts, so a later row with the same date must replace the earlier one. C15's code-301 fail/pass on 2026-02-01 depends on it: with `>` C15 would lose P07 and P10.

Negating the rating gives highest-first inside an ascending sort, `date.max` puts blank join dates last, and the id is the final tie-break: exactly rule 5. It looks like it could invert the order, but it doesn't.

bugs.title: Only the first required course is checked
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_chat_safety: P02 gets ['C01', 'C04'] instead of ['C01', 'C10']. Every other project is unchanged.
bugs.why: `return None` sits inside the for loop, so missing_course returns after looking at the first course only. C04 has core-101 but their latest safety-201 attempt is a fail, and they become eligible for P02 and outrank C10 on rating. P08 is unaffected because it lists pii-110 first, and nobody without core-101 holds pii-110.
hints: Look up C04 in courses.csv. Which P02 course do they hold right now?
Look at how missing_course walks the project's course list.
The `return None` is indented into the loop; dedent it so every course is checked.
probes: P08 also lists two courses. Why did it come out right with the early return in place?
C04 is free again after the fix. Why doesn't that change any later project?

bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_multi_project_contributors: all 16 contributors appear, inactive and unstaffed ones included, each with the same long list of every pick made so far (it keeps growing with each build_report call in the test run). The assignments themselves are correct.
bugs.why: `projects = []` is a class attribute, so every Contributor's `self.projects.append(...)` writes into one shared list. Hours are tracked per instance, so staffing still works and only the report built from `projects` is affected.
hints: Even C07, who is inactive, shows up in multi_project. Where does that list come from?
Look at where a Contributor's `projects` list is created.
Remove the class-level `projects = []` and set `self.projects = []` in __init__.
probes: Why did hours_left keep working per contributor when projects didn't?
Why would the list have grown even further if build_report ran twice in one process?

context_qa.q: What happens inside build_report, in order?
context_qa.a: It loads contributors, attaches each contributor's latest course results with `rules.attach_courses`, loads projects, runs `assigner.staff`, computes course demand from the projects, and builds the report dict (assignments, open_seats, multi_project, course_demand, top_course).

context_qa.q: How does staff() choose people for one project?
context_qa.a: For projects with seats > 0 it filters all contributors with `is_eligible`, sorts them by `rank_key`, and takes the first `seats`. Each pick subtracts `hours_per_seat` from `hours_left`, appends the project id to `contributor.projects`, and adds the contributor id to the project's list.

context_qa.q: What does is_eligible check, and in what order?
context_qa.a: Active flag first, then the locale (only if the project has one), then `missing_course(contributor, project.courses)` must be None, and finally `hours_left >= hours_per_seat`.

context_qa.q: Where do contributor.courses values come from?
context_qa.a: `attach_courses` calls `latest_results` on every CourseResult row and stores `result` (a lower-cased string such as 'pass' or 'fail') under `contributors[cid].courses[course]`, skipping ids that aren't in contributors.csv.
From each Contributor object's `projects` list after staffing: contributors sorted by id, kept if `len(c.projects) >= 2`, with the list sorted.

context_qa.q: How does the loader handle a blank rating?
context_qa.a: `_number` returns None for a blank cell and a float otherwise. The rating passed to Contributor is then derived from that value and the module-level `DEFAULT_RATING` (3.0).
